sources.title: Map, Filter, and Conquer: A Visual Tool for Learning Higher-Order Functions
sources.language: Algot versus Python/Jupyter; Haskell not measured
sources.design: Randomized order, within-subject crossover; two hours; two tutorials up to 45 minutes, four HOFs; first-attempt implementation, behavior questions and Paas effort.
sources.findings: Reported effort 4.78 versus 6.04, d=1.03, p<.001; implementation errors 1.33 versus 2.89. Excluding Python syntax errors gives 1.70 and nonsignificant difference, p=.058. Behavioral questions also nonsignificant. Time 16.8 versus 25.6 minutes.
sources.limitations: Brief intervention, carryover despite distractor, selected tasks, first-attempt scoring; procedural tool performance is not retention/transfer. Self-reported load; syntax protection confounds conceptual benefit.

sources.title: Teaching types with a cognitively effective worked example format
sources.design: Repeated single-subject A-B-A; textbook baseline, five worked derivations plus deduction rules, then baseline; early master-level FP course.
sources.findings: Specific individuals confused application/abstraction, type-variable scope across signatures, currying and type classes. Beginner gains with derivations had mixed maintenance; advanced students had little scope to improve. Prototype analogy survey 9/18 yes, including explanations.
sources.limitations: Exploratory volunteers, no general validation; repeated tasks and stricter intervention scoring, protocol deviations, extra individual correction, omitted hardest questions. Pilot versus volunteer accounting unclear; no long-term retention.

sources.title: Developing Behavioral Concepts of Higher-Order Functions
sources.language: Racket preparation; Pyret semester; no Haskell comparison
sources.design: Five optional clustering/classification stages; first four over month, fifth three months later; behavioral examples/diagrams.
sources.findings: Filter/take-while distinctions remained harder than map/filter; fold's universality complicates classifications. Stage 5 persistence supports targeted behavioral probes. Authors recommend justifications and learner-generated examples; diagram superiority not established.
sources.limitations: Changing samples; Stage 4 identities missing; no matched retention estimate or causal instruction comparison. Small HOF set, ambiguous examples, prior exposure, optional participation; recognition not coding or constructing function arguments.

sources.title: Observations on the Design of Program Planning Notations for Students
sources.language: Data-centric FP table operations, Snap! planning; later Python; exact FP language not named in inspected paper
sources.design: Two consecutive novice-course offerings: Fall 2022 blocks and Spring 2023 free-form paper; work artifacts, optional feedback and interviews.
sources.findings: Earlier experienced-student block-planning success did not carry over cleanly. Novices described rigid/time-consuming planning; many supplied code-like plans or completed plans after coding. Paper plans favored to-do lists; mechanisms for composing subtasks remained underspecified.
sources.limitations: Experience report, cohort/task changes and self-selection; no causal learning comparison or complete Spring denominator. Interviews concern selected mixed-notation users; inspect expectations and practical benefit before imposing a planner.

sources.design: Mirrored abstract describes multiple-choice items in online introductory FP course; primary methods unavailable.
sources.abstract_lead_only: Abstract names polymorphism/subtyping confusion, excessive significance assigned to variable names, and conflating general patterns with special cases. These are leads, not independently verified prevalence claims.
sources.limitations: ACM DOI inaccessible; ResearchGate says no full text; OpenAlex no OA location. Primary sample, language, items and coding unverified.
